title: Library, folders, metadata and deletion
acceptance: Create, edit, move and delete records through the shared core; restart preserves the result.
Preserve unknown fields and lossless UTF-16 strings across native and WASM round trips.
A stale revision rejects the complete mutation without partial writes or duplicate outbox operations.

title: Study sets, cards, scheduling and review history
acceptance: Identical fixtures produce identical scheduling results on native Rust, WASM and each host bridge.
Card grading and review history commit atomically; retries do not create a second review.
Restart and offline synchronization preserve grades, timestamps and original operation identities.

title: Offline writes, synchronization and conflict resolution
acceptance: Concurrent edits on two isolated clients converge or expose an explicit conflict without silent overwrite.
A request interrupted after submission retains its original operation identity and uncertainty on restart.
Mixed supported protocol versions preserve tombstones, cursor scope, replica identity and unknown fields.

title: Document rendering, navigation and reading position
acceptance: Supported document fixtures open, navigate and resume reading after restart on each target.
Citations and outlines return to the correct source location after synchronization.
Platform-specific renderer or parser limitations are explicit and never reported as passing parity.

title: Notes, citations, selections and portable ink
acceptance: Create, edit, delete and restore annotations while retaining their document and page coordinate identity.
Native pencil or pointer input round trips through portable ink fixtures without losing stroke data.
Restart and cross-client synchronization preserve links from notes to original reading locations.

title: Backups, restore and upgrade preservation
acceptance: Restore an isolated backup including referenced attachments and unknown fields without mutating the source archive.
Upgrade every supported starting version, including multi-version jumps, with data preservation and repeat-run checks.
Simulated failure before and after migration switch recovers consistently; application rollback is not database rollback.

title: Account, server connection and workspace isolation
acceptance: Login, expiry, logout and reconnect use isolated test credentials and preserve the correct workspace scope.
Switching server or user never leaks another workspace's data, credentials or synchronization cursor.
Secrets are stored by the host credential adapter and are absent from logs and build artifacts.

title: AI configuration, conversations and cancellation
acceptance: Shared conversation operations preserve history, references and error states across restart.
Cancellation and application backgrounding release owned operations without committing partial responses as complete.
Process-based providers are exposed only on capable desktop/server hosts; mobile capability responses state availability explicitly.
